source.note: Brief is source evidence, not an instruction to start building in this setup session. User additionally requires public repo and no publication yet.

A3-01.title: Verify startup and shared service contracts

A3-02.title: Generate and play an instrumental from the UI

A3-03.title: Generate vocal songs with AI lyrics

A3-04.title: Generate and pair a new cover for every song

A3-05.title: Play a queue with the default AI DJ and controls

A3-06.title: Support MP3 and WAV DJ reference voices safely

A3-07.title: Ship three class-generated sample tracks and covers

A3-08.title: Verify failure recovery and public-file safeguards

A3-09.title: Maintain verified README, screenshots and findings

A3-10.title: Rehearse ZIP installation and freeze the submission

A3-GH.title: Publish the public repo and verify main protection

AT-01.title: Starter and team decisions
AT-01.expected: Original starter wording retained; team additions/choices are separate and checked.

AT-02.title: Real class service contracts
AT-02.expected: Four prescribed services accept documented feature requests, with class-only config, no paid features and no app request to port 9000.

AT-03.title: Instrumental song
AT-03.expected: Normal launch: style/mood/duration -> playable ACE-Step instrumental -> session library.

AT-04.title: Vocal song
AT-04.expected: Qwen AI lyrics -> playable ACE-Step vocal song using selected settings.

AT-05.title: New matching covers
AT-05.expected: New FLUX covers reflect song context and remain paired with two or more distinct tracks.

AT-06.title: Session library
AT-06.expected: Newly generated tracks remain selectable/playable for the session through later generation and playback.

AT-07.title: Default AI DJ
AT-07.expected: Without an upload, Qwen track-specific commentary is spoken by Chatterbox between queued songs.

AT-08.title: Reference DJ voices
AT-08.expected: Both MP3 and WAV uploads customize DJ speech; default mode and temporary cleanup still work.

AT-09.title: Playback sequencing
AT-09.expected: Pause/resume, skip, automatic advancement, speech then music without overlap, including transition races.

AT-10.title: Status, failure and recovery
AT-10.expected: Generation progress is visible; at least one failed request produces a useful safe error and a working recovery.

AT-11.title: Three ready samples
AT-11.expected: Three actual titled class-generated songs/covers ship, play, and have honest AI-lyric/generation provenance.

AT-12.title: Public-file safeguards
AT-12.expected: No credentials exposed; uploads/voice references excluded from Git/ZIP; no bundled third-party music, lyrics, art or voices.

AT-13.title: Verified setup and use documentation
AT-13.expected: README has dependencies/software, secure config examples, launch/use of all core features and real screenshots; team verifies wording against app.

AT-14.title: Honest feature/failure evidence
AT-14.expected: Inputs, expected and actual results for all three features plus a failure distinguish passed, failed and unchecked claims.

AT-15.title: Design judgment and limitation
AT-15.expected: One important choice is justified by observed tests; an investigated limitation/failure and lesson are explained.

AT-16.title: Independent ZIP deployment
AT-16.expected: Another teammate installs this exact GitHub ZIP using only README/class keys, exercises core flows and samples, and resolves missing-file/setup issues.

AT-17.title: Team participation
AT-17.expected: Every actual teammate has a meaningful contribution and a completed review of a teammate, with evidence.

AT-18.title: Submission identity and access
AT-18.expected: Public repo is accessible through grading; repo URL, exact merged commit, GitHub ZIP and required files agree.

AT-19.title: Public repository access
AT-19.expected: Public repo access and protected main are verified after authorization; the team keeps access available through grading.

requirements.statement: Retain all existing starter language; team reviews/adds instructions.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B port 9001 supplies text generation.
FLUX.2 klein 4B port 9006 supplies cover art.
ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo port 9007 supplies music.
Chatterbox Multilingual V3 port 9008 supplies DJ speech.
Use supplied connection details and documented service request formats.
Core uses class credentials alone; no paid features, including optional ones; no app requests to port 9000.
Choose song style, mood and duration.
Generate playable instrumental music and add it to the library.
Generate playable vocal tracks with AI-generated lyrics.
Generate new matching FLUX art per custom song; display with correct track and reflect theme/style/mood.
Newly generated songs join the playable library and remain available during the session.
Qwen writes song-specific commentary spoken by Chatterbox between queued songs.
Default DJ voice works without upload.
MP3 reference customizes the DJ voice.
WAV reference customizes the DJ voice.
Include three ready-to-play sample songs with titles and covers.
Pregenerate samples with class endpoints; any lyrics are AI-generated; explain sample generation.
Provide play and pause controls.
Provide skip controls.
After playback starts, advance automatically with sequential speech/music and no overlap.
Show generation status, understandable errors and recovery from failed requests.
Credentials server-side; absent from GitHub, archives, browser code, logs and docs; placeholder examples.
Never commit user uploads or voice-reference recordings, or include them in submission archives.
Do not bundle third-party music, lyrics, cover art or voice samples.
README starts report/docs: dependencies, software, secure endpoint config, launch and use of all core features.
Include screenshots illustrating interface and core features.
Record inputs/expected/actual for three features and at least one failure; disclose unresolved/unchecked claims.
Explain an important design choice justified with test evidence.
Investigate a limitation/failure and explain what was learned.
Team verifies documentation against finished app and explains findings in its own words.
Submit one shared repo link, exact commit and GitHub-downloaded ZIP of that same version per team on Canvas.
ZIP contains code, dependencies, config examples, docs and actual generated sample audio/images needed to run.
Teammate independently installs extracted ZIP from docs/class keys, tests core features and fixes missing/private-machine dependencies.
GitHub issues/PRs organize/review substantial work; every teammate contributes meaningfully and reviews a teammate.
Repository stays accessible through grading; user additionally requires public visibility.
